g1_mech#3.closest: Grasberg underground block-cave crusher/conveyor system (phase 1 commissioned mid-2018), Freeport-McMoRan; the Vale S11D truck-free in-pit crush-and-convey system is the open-pit analogue
g1_mech#3.url: https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/15/24/13148 (Grasberg snippet came from the bulk-online result; the S11D figures are from https://www.flsmidth.com/-/media/brochures/performance-studies/batch1/fls-performance-study_22-027f.pdf)
g1_mech#3.same: Crush then belt in place of trucks; the Metso blog and the AusIMM paper put belt energy at 15–30% of truck energy, which matches the 3–5x claim
g1_mech#3.new: A level-scale crusher feeding a fixed belt to the shaft at Talnakh, in narrow-vein sulphide ore, with Russian belts and Ruselprom drives. I found no Talnakh or Norilsk source. The search was thin on underground-specific work.

g1_neg#2.closest: Kutcho Copper project pre-sorting plan (Canada, ~2020s); NexMetals Selebi Cu-Ni XRT bulk tests
g1_neg#2.same: XRT sorting of sulphide ore ahead of the mill, with sorter rejects used as cemented backfill in underground mines. NexMetals reported head grade up more than 15% on Cu-Ni-Co ore. A 2026 paper reports 95.67% Cu recovery.
g1_neg#2.new: Sorting at the shaft bottom of a disseminated Ni-Cu mine (Norilsk), domestic sorters, the stated aim of freeing fixed concentrator capacity, and the <3% metal-loss target. Kutcho is a plan, not an operating case.

g1_rf1#2.closest: Novatek Arc7 shuttles to the Saam FSU near Murmansk, with ship-to-ship transfer to conventional tankers, 2026
g1_rf1#2.same: Arc7 ships load at Gydan or Yamal and unload to Saam, then conventional tankers carry the cargo. Novatek plans a ~4-day turnaround for winter Gulf of Ob–Murmansk shuttles. Arc7 STS transfers at Kildin are also reported.
g1_rf1#2.new: Nothing material. Only the quantified 1.5–2x cargo gain and the turnaround-logging test are not in the sources.

g1_neg#3.closest: Larsen, "Integrated post and jack system", US 2011/0088336, and Canadian patent CA 2717101
g1_neg#3.same: A hydraulic leveling jack on a post base, for foundations hit by subsidence and frost heave in permafrost, used to re-level after movement. The Alaska 2022 guide and NREL 2024 guidebook call adjustable foundations standard, and say jacks on piles correct differential settlement.
g1_neg#3.new: Survey-driven re-levelling on a schedule, 300 mm stroke, and application to industrial plant on spread footings or space frames. The ground is allowed to thaw. Industrial use is only weakly covered.

g1_rf1#1.closest: Yamal LNG Train 4, Novatek Arctic Cascade, 0.9 Mtpa, domestic equipment, started 2021
g1_rf1#1.same: The same unit, using Russian-made equipment and the cold climate to cut liquefaction cost. Novatek originally meant to reuse it elsewhere.
g1_rf1#1.new: Series copies of 3 trains sharing the GBS, port and berths at Utrenneye and Sabetta, and the <$600/t/y capex target. Reports say Novatek dropped reuse of the technology at Ob LNG. Train 4 was delayed by commissioning problems with the domestic equipment.

g1_rf2#3.same: Borehole-temperature ranking of Norilsk foundations, with a modelled pile capacity loss of up to 50% over 60 years. Thermosyphons on piles were seven-year monitored on the Qinghai–Tibet line.
